title: Synthetic Data-Based Simulators for Recommender Systems: A Survey
summary: Surveys simulators that stand in for live recommender systems during development, decomposing them into four components — synthetic user and item profiles, a response function, a feedback loop, and an evaluation procedure — and comparing published simulators on which components each supplies and how each handles real-world drift in user behaviour. SDV is cited twice: as the library SynEvaRec calls to build synthetic user and item profiles with Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and CopulaGAN, and as a source of ready-made metrics for judging generated data quality, grouped into statistical, likelihood and detection families; the survey itself runs nothing.
evidence: section on synthetic profile generation states that SynEvaRec uses the existing library for synthetic data generation SDV (Patki et al. 2016) to create synthetic profiles of users and items with Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and CopulaGAN models; the evaluation component section proposes assessing synthetic data quality with metrics from the SDV library, divided into statistical, likelihood and detection groups; the SDV DSAA 2016 paper is the cited anchor and no experiment in the survey uses it

title: Improving Correlation Capture in Generating Imbalanced Data using Differentially Private Conditional GANs
summary: Proposes DP-CGANS, a conditional GAN for tabular data whose conditional vector is built to preserve correlations between variables rather than only marginal distributions, trained under differential privacy so that the synthetic records carry a stated privacy cost. Its continuous-column encoder is the mode-specific normalization proposed in the CTGAN paper, adopted directly; CTGAN is one of the three GAN frameworks it is measured against; and the whole comparison is run inside SDGym, the SDV project's benchmarking suite, which supplies the utility and privacy metrics reported.
evidence: the model section states that continuous variables are transformed using mode-specific normalization proposed by Xu et al., the CTGAN reference; the related-work section credits CTGAN with inventing training-by-sampling for imbalanced categorical variables alongside the conditional vector; section 4.1 compares DP-CGANS against CTGAN, MedGAN and TableGAN using the benchmarking suite developed by Synthetic Data Gym, footnoted to github.com/sdv-dev/SDGym, which supplies the data utility and privacy metrics

title: Design Target Achievement Index: A Differentiable Metric to Enhance Deep Generative Models in Multi-Objective Inverse Design
summary: Observes that deep generative models in engineering design optimise for statistical resemblance to the training set rather than for meeting a designer's targets, and proposes the Design Target Achievement Index, a differentiable score over multiple objectives and constraints that can be added to a generative model's loss so that sampling is steered toward feasible designs that hit the targets. CTGAN and TVAE are the two tabular generators it benchmarks against on parametric bicycle-frame data, chosen as the established state of the art for the GAN and VAE classes respectively.
evidence: the abstract reports comparative performance against baseline deep generative models including specialized tabular generation algorithms like the Conditional Tabular GAN; the methods section states the paper tests TVAE and CTGAN introduced by Xu et al. in 2019, noting both established state-of-the-art performance on tabular data generation for their respective model classes

title: ConvGeN: Convex space learning improves deep-generative oversampling for tabular imbalanced classification on smaller datasets
summary: Argues that deep oversamplers trained adversarially need more data than small imbalanced tables provide, and proposes ConvGeN, which learns convex combinations of minority neighbourhoods so that generated points stay inside the convex space of the minority class and remain separable from the majority. CTGAN is one of the two tabular generators it is measured against: the paper runs it from the sdv-dev repository, describes its conditional vector and packing discriminator, and automates the discrete-versus-continuous column declaration it requires, reporting that on smaller datasets CTGAN performs worse than the non-generative baseline.
evidence: section IV.D gives the CTGAN git link as github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN and describes its non-Gaussian modelling, conditional vector and packing discriminator; the same section states that to train CTGAN a list of discrete columns must be supplied and that the authors automated this decision by integer-versus-fractional column typing; the results report that CTGAN and CTAB-GAN in most cases perform worse than the baseline on smaller tabular datasets

title: Generating Synthetic Population
summary: Builds a synthetic population for India at several administrative levels by combining census, IHDS-II, NSS and gridded population sources, assigning individuals to households and households to administrative units so that the result can seed agent-based simulation. CTGAN is one of the generators trialled for producing the base population and is reported as rejected in favour of iterative proportional updating, on the ground that IPU can match individual-level and household-level characteristics simultaneously while CTGAN cannot.
evidence: the methods section names Iterative Proportional Fitting, Iterative Proportional Updating and a specialized neural network called Conditional-Tabular Generative Adversarial Network by Xu et al. as the techniques used to generate new data; a later passage states the authors also experimented with CTGAN to generate a base population and that the major advantage of IPU over CTGAN is IPU's ability to match individual-level and household-level characteristics at once

title: G2A2: An Automated Graph Generator with Attributes and Anomalies
summary: Addresses the shortage of dynamic attributed graph datasets carrying anomaly ground truth by generating them: a temporal bipartite graph is produced first, anomalies are injected to emulate burstiness and propagation, and node attributes are then synthesised and mapped onto the graph. CTGAN performs that last stage, run as two separate instances trained on the normal and anomalous partitions of a source table so that the attributes attached to injected anomalies come from the anomalous distribution.
evidence: the overview states that by leveraging deep generative models like CTGAN the pipeline generates and maps realistic attributes to the graph; the attribute-generation section states that two conditional tabular generative adversarial networks are used, with the source dataset divided into normal and anomalous parts so each instance learns the corresponding attribute distribution
